transcript.text: I'd like to share my patient assessment findings now so everyone has this context ahead of the 2:00 PM readiness check. The South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt, according to my therapy assessment. This means the South unit patient has a clear clinical need for the bariatric lift, while the North unit patient has an alternative safe transfer method available.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'd like to share my equipment specifications ahead of the 2:00 PM readiness check as well. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, and its 48-inch turning radius fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway. North room 318 has a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. The charger must therefore be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. This means that from a facilities and equipment standpoint, the lift can only be safely used on the South unit.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I'd like to share my staff competency validation information ahead of the 2:00 PM readiness check as well. Three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation, and hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer. Their available coverage is 07:00-19:00 daily. This means the South unit has the required validated staff to safely perform lift transfers within that coverage window.
